newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - May 9.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name products and Consumer Trends.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Communication, information technology, telecommunications, television and multmedia will be the top business areas of the next century, but of all these, the one facing the greatest challenge is advertising. It must adapt or die, says Jacques Seguela, vice chairman of Havas Advertising and an advertising guru in France. (Strategies)

PARIS - France faces the dilemma of breaking its own laws or depriving French TV viewers of seeing next year's World Cup finals if it allows U.S. brewer Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc, which has signed a 100 million-franc ($17.4 million) contract with world soccer body FIFA for the right to advertise its Budweiser beer in the World Cup stadiums during the tournament here next year.(Reuter)

PARIS - The number of people who watch television at least once a day in France rose in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period last year, French audience measurement body Mediametrie says, denying recent press reports of a sharp decline. (Reuter)

PARIS - Jean-Bernard Ichac, strategy and development director at TF1 Publicite, the advertising arm of private television channel TF1, says audiences shrank in the first quarter, but the shrinkage was small compared to 1996, a record high year for television audiences. (Le Figaro)

PARIS - Elf Aquitaine changes its advertising message. The oil company has picked BDDP for its next campaign, to run from Monday, centred on showing Elf's involvement with current issues. (Le Figaro).
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
PARIS - Television par Satellite (TPS) reacts to rival Canal Plus snapping up new French film production by planning to spend 100 million francs on pre-buying French films. (Le Figaro)

WARSAW - French firm Hachette has asked a Warsaw court to rule whether its initial deal on buying press chain Ruch SA, signed in December but later annuled, is legally binding, PAP news agency says. (Reuter)

CANNES - Britain's Gary Oldman packs an explosive punch with his film, "Nil by Mouth", the first to run at the Cannes film festival, and won widespread acclaim for its partly autobiographical portrait of a family that holds together only thanks to its women. (Reuter)
PARIS - The French have been slow to catch the Internet/multimedia bug but nearly a fifth plan to connect in the next two years and to buy multimedia equipment, a recent study shows. (Reuter)
PARIS - Cable television is watched in 23.8 percent of cabled homes in France, a significant rise since December 1995, a study published by audience measurement body Mediametrie says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - Mineral water brand Vittel's poster advertising campaign wins the IPSOS-Strategies campaign of the week, with a recognition score of 46 percent. Volvo's press campaign gets a top rating by a panel of advertising creatives for Teleperformance's measurement of the top 10 campaigns. (Strategies).
PARIS - French industry minister Franck Borotra says a merger between the two French car groups Renault and PSA Peugot Citroen would be "a very bad idea". (Reuter)

PARIS - Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel said a three percent decline in passenger cars carried on its shuttle service in April compared to March was partly because there were fewer weekends in April. (Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
